report.narrative_markdown:
## Company overview

Apple Inc. designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories worldwide. Its product lines include iPhone, Mac, iPad, and a wearables, home and accessories group that covers AirPods, Apple Vision Pro, Apple TV, Apple Watch, Beats products and HomePod. It also provides AppleCare support, cloud services and platforms such as the App Store. Apple sits in the Consumer Electronics industry within the Technology sector, with a market capitalization of $4.91T, and its shares trade at $336.64 against a 52-week range of 243.42-345.34.

## Financial commentary

Revenue was $394.33B in fiscal 2022, slipped to $383.29B in 2023, recovered to $391.04B in 2024 and reached $416.16B in 2025. Net income followed a different path: $99.80B in 2022, $97.00B in 2023 and $93.74B in 2024, before rising to $112.01B in 2025. The latest year therefore marks a high point for both lines over the period shown.

Profitability is strong, with a net margin of 27.6% and a return on equity of 148.8%. Revenue growth is given as 16.4%. Debt/Equity stands at 0.78 and the dividend yield is 0.3%, which indicates that shareholder returns come mainly through the share price rather than the payout.

## Comps commentary

Compared with the peer median, Apple trades at a premium on every valuation multiple supplied. Its forward P/E of 35.1 is 73% above the peer median of 20.3, and its trailing P/E of 38.6 is 94% above the median of 19.9. EV/EBITDA of 29.4 is 42% above the median of 20.7, while EV/Revenue of 10.6 is 303% above the median of 2.6.

On operating measures, Apple's net margin of 27.6% is 267% above the peer median of 7.5%, and its Debt/Equity of 0.78 is 268% above the median of 0.21. Revenue growth of 16.4% is 7% below the peer median of 17.7%. The peer set is mixed, spanning large software and internet platforms as well as hardware makers, so the median should be read with caution. In short, the market is paying a higher multiple for Apple's margins and scale, not for faster growth.

## Company overview

JPMorgan Chase & Co. is a bank and financial holding company in the Financial Services sector, classed within Banks - Diversified. It operates across the United States, the rest of North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia Pacific, Latin America and the Caribbean. Its business is organised into three segments: Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management. Products include deposits, investment and lending products, cash management, mortgage origination and servicing, home equity loans, credit cards, payment solutions and auto loans. With a market capitalisation of $885.15B, it is a very large participant in its industry.

## Financial commentary

Revenue rose each year over the period shown, from $127.73B in 2022 to $154.95B in 2023, $169.44B in 2024 and $181.85B in 2025. Net income climbed from $37.68B in 2022 to $49.55B in 2023 and $58.47B in 2024, then eased to $57.05B in 2025, so earnings dipped slightly in the latest year even as revenue grew.

The company reports a net margin of 34.9%, a return on equity of 17.8% and revenue growth of 30.4%. The shares trade at $332.99, within a 52-week range of 279.10 to 366.50. The dividend yield is 2.0%.

## Comps commentary

The comparison uses financial-sector peers: Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley. The primary multiple is price-to-book, where JPMorgan stands at 2.5 against a peer median of 1.5, a premium of 63%. On forward P/E it trades at 13.3 versus 10.4, a 27% premium, while its trailing P/E of 14.3 is only 3% above the peer median of 13.8.

The premium is accompanied by stronger operating metrics. Return on equity of 17.8% is 41% above the peer median of 12.6%, and revenue growth of 30.4% is 81% above the median of 16.8%. The dividend yield of 2.0% is 16% below the peer median of 2.4%. Overall, the market is pricing JPMorgan above most of its peers, a valuation that coincides with its higher profitability and growth.
